cases.description: Octet equals PAD_DEFAULT ('='). The method should return true via the first OR condition.
Octet is a valid Base64 character ('A'). It is within the decode table range and DECODE_TABLE[65] = 0 (not -1), so the method returns true.
Octet is the last lowercase Base64 character ('z'). It is in range and maps to 51, therefore the method returns true.
Octet is a space character, which is within the table range but maps to -1. The method should fall through to false.
Octet is the null byte (0). It is in range but DECODE_TABLE[0] = -1, so the method returns false.
Octet is negative. The first part of the second condition (octet >= 0) fails, leading to a false result.
Octet is the highest possible byte value (DEL). It is within the array length but maps to -1, so the method returns false.
Octet is '+' (ASCII 43), a valid Base64 character mapping to 62. Should return true.
Octet is '-' (ASCII 45), a valid Base64 character (URL‑safe variant) mapping to 62. Should return true.
Octet is '/' (ASCII 47), a valid Base64 character mapping to 63. Should return true.
Octet is '_' (ASCII 95), a valid URL‑safe Base64 character mapping to 63. Should return true.
Octet is '0' (ASCII 48), a valid Base64 digit mapping to 52. Should return true.
Octet is '9' (ASCII 57), a valid Base64 digit mapping to 61. Should return true.
Octet is '@' (ASCII 64), not part of Base64 alphabet. Should return false.
Octet is '[' (ASCII 91), not part of Base64 alphabet. Should return false.
Octet is ']' (ASCII 93), not part of Base64 alphabet. Should return false.
Octet is '|' (ASCII 124), not part of Base64 alphabet. Should return false.
Octet is the minimum byte value (-128). Negative values cause the first part of the second condition to fail, returning false.
Octet is '~' (ASCII 126), not a Base64 character. Should return false.
Octet is '?' (ASCII 63), not a Base64 character. Should return false.
Octet is '{' (ASCII 123), not a Base64 character. Should return false.
